x-k-k3-01.title: Who give pocket money?
x-k-k3-01.topic: Subjects left out: who they mean
x-k-k3-01.goal: Guess who omitted subject refer to, point to text clues and explain how guess change if one clue disappear.
x-k-k3-01.material:
Two classmates, 지우 and 하나, dey chat using polite -요 speech. Korean often leave out subject (person doing action). (댁 = respectful word for somebody house.)

지우: 어제 뭐 했어요?
하나: 할머니 댁에 갔어요. 맛있는 밥을 먹었어요. 용돈도 주셨어요.
지우: 좋았겠어요!
x-k-k3-01.thinking.0: Guess an unstated subject from several clues
x-k-k3-01.thinking.2: Change guess if one clue disappear
x-k-k3-01.prereq.1: Know -요 endings and words 할머니, 친구, 용돈
x-k-k3-01.s.s1.prompt: Who give 하나 pocket money (용돈도 주셨어요)?
x-k-k3-01.s.s1.hint.0: Check ending of 주셨어요 and compare with 먹었어요 in line before.
x-k-k3-01.s.s1.hint.1: List every person wey appear in 하나 three sentences.
x-k-k3-01.s.s1.r.a: She na person wey receive money, and verb wey honor doer no use for yourself.
x-k-k3-01.s.s1.r.c: 지우 only ask and react; text no say e give anything.
x-k-k3-01.s.s1.r.d: Verb form point to someone she respect, no be same-age classmate.
x-k-k3-01.s.s1.explain: Text no name subject, but verb form show giver na person wey deserve respect, and only that person in story na 할머니, whose house 하나 visit. ‘Probably’ fit because text no state am directly.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.prompt: Which pieces of evidence support your answer? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.hint.0: For each option, ask: e tell me WHO or only WETIN?
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.hint.1: Find one clue from verb and one clue from place.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.o.a: 용돈 mean pocket money, so giver must be family member.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.r.a: Word name wetin dem give, no be who give am.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.o.b: 맛있는 밥 show giver also cook meal.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.r.b: Food and money na different actions; nothing connect dem to one person.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.o.c: 주셨어요 get form wey show respect for person doing action.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.o.d: 하나 just dey at 할머니 house and nobody else dey mentioned there.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.explain: Two clues work together: verb form tell what kind of person giver be, and story show who dey there. Pocket money and food no tell who giver be.
x-k-k3-01.s.s2.acc.0: Verb form na strongest single clue; d add say story context fit am.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.prompt: Imagine 하나 talk ‘용돈도 줬어요’ instead of ‘용돈도 주셨어요’. Wetin change?
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.hint.0: Remove clue from s2 wey you find strongest and see wetin remain.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.hint.1: Ask which people still fit be giver.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.o.a: Nothing change; giver still clearly 할머니.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.r.a: Honorific form na one clue wey narrow down giver; without am, clue disappear.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.o.b: Giver fit now also be friend or younger person.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.r.c: Nothing in text point to 지우 either way.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.r.d: ‘줬어요’ normal polite sentence; e just carry less information about giver.
x-k-k3-01.s.s3.explain: Without honorific form, story still fit 할머니, but e no rule out other people. You suppose be less certain about first answer.

x-k-k3-02.title: One strange line in self-introduction

x-k-k3-02.material: New student, 이민수, introduce himself to class. Five lines shown. One line sound strange to Korean listener.

x-k-k3-02.s.s1.hint.1: Look at wetin come right after name.

x-k-k3-02.s.s2.hint.0: Think when you add 님: 선생님? 친구? Yourself?

x-k-k3-02.s.s2.o.a: Respectful title attach to speaker own name.
x-k-k3-02.s.s2.o.b: Names fit only get 은/는 after dem, never 이에요.
x-k-k3-02.s.s2.r.b: 이에요 after name normal way to say ‘I am ___’; that no be problem.
x-k-k3-02.s.s2.o.c: Introduction must use 입니다, never 이에요.
x-k-k3-02.s.s2.r.c: Both polite; line 5 use 습니다 and line 1 use 요, and mixing dem normal.

x-k-k3-02.s.s2.r.d: Full name normal; issue na what come after name.

x-k-k3-03.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite message for 할머니 in Korean. Start by calling her 할머니.

Pen pal 서준 write you:

x-k-k3-04.s.s1.prompt: 서준 wan know about you and your family. Which reply give clearest picture?

x-k-k3-04.s.s1.r.b: E describe parents jobs but leave out writer name, age and comparison like 서준 own.

x-k-k3-04.s.s2.prompt: Write your own reply in Korean (4-5 short sentences). Include name, age, at least one family member, and one comparison with 보다 (e.g. who older or younger than you). Use polite style.

민호 wrote:
